summary: For an answer longer than a line. Input's sibling; the same wiring, more room.

pairs.dont: Fix the height and let content scroll inside it.
pairs.do: Set a minimum and let the field grow.
pairs.why: A box that cannot grow is why people write three words where they meant three sentences — they cannot see what they have written, so they stop. field-sizing-content does this without JavaScript.

pairs.dont: Leave the browser default resize, which drags both ways.
pairs.why: A textarea dragged wider breaks the column it sits in, and nobody has ever needed a wider one. Vertical is the axis people actually want.

pairs.dont: Use a Textarea for a name, an ID or a threshold.
pairs.why: The size of the box is a promise about the length of the answer. A three-line box under "Probe name" invites a paragraph, and then something downstream has to truncate it.

pairs.do: State the limit, and show the count as it approaches.
pairs.why: A field that stops accepting characters without explanation reads as broken. If the limit matters enough to enforce, it matters enough to say.

pairs.do: Let read-only drop the resize handle along with the editing.
pairs.why: A resize handle is an affordance for editing. On a field nobody can edit it is a control that does nothing, which is worse than no control.

a11y: Wrap it in Field so the label, hint and error are wired — Textarea takes the same FieldControl as Input.
aria-invalid rather than a prop, so the failure reaches assistive tech at the same moment the border turns red.
field-sizing-content is Chrome-only today; elsewhere the minimum height plus the native resize handle is the fallback, which is what people already expect.
